verdicts.note: Vocabulary outcomes in dual language learners.

Published AJAE version of 'Curse of the Mummy-ji': mothers-in-law constraining young married women's networks, mobility and reproductive health in patrilocal India. Keep this over the RePEc preprint in batch 21.
Occupational zoonoses in Southeast Asia; 'close proximity' is human-animal.

'HOUSING AS A FERTILITY TRAP' -- housing finance and policy in East Central Europe explicitly to understand the connection between housing, INDEPENDENT HOUSEHOLD FORMATION, and demographic outcomes. Wall 1's mechanism named as the title of the paper, in a region the frame is thin on. Second-read packet.
Caregiver attitudes to children's dental visits.

'Counting on POTENTIAL GRANDPARENTS?' -- whether would-be grandparents' PROPENSITY to care predicts adult children's ENTRY INTO PARENTHOOD across Europe, Demography. Uses the propensity rather than realised care, which is the same endogeneity fix as the living-status paper in batch 18. C.2.a's exposure, but the design is one this chapter should borrow.

"'We're Fine at Home': Young People, Family and Low Fertility in SPAIN" -- fieldwork on how young Spaniards understand their own role in the birth-rate decline. Qualitative, and the title states the mechanism §1 hypothesises from the inside: staying is comfortable, not merely constrained.
Minimum income standards for older people in Singapore.
Ravenstein's laws and step migration in Victorian England.
Institutions and immutable determinants of human capital.
Indirect consequences of COVID-19 in France, Italy and Spain.

Gated anchor, in its Vienna Yearbook debate form: 'MOVING OUT THE PARENTAL HOME AND PARTNERSHIP FORMATION AS SOCIAL DETERMINANTS OF LOW FERTILITY'. The registered hypothesis stated as a position in a field debate; the other contributions to the same debate are separate records in this batch and route out.
Companion contribution to the same Vienna Yearbook debate; international political economy and fertility.
Same debate; gender and social stratification. D.2.a's.
Parental readiness among Japanese nursing students.
Same debate; marriage as the key to East Asian fertility. A.7's, but it is the position the extended arm has to argue against in Japan.
Health impact of a fuel-poverty programme.
Same debate; compressed modernity and millennial values. D.1.a's.
Encyclopedia entry on culture and social development.
Same debate; ideal family size and empowerment.
Japanese marriage and family change, with marriage and childbirth still tightly coupled. Context for why the pre-launch and extended configurations are hard to separate in Japan.
Early-adulthood transitions including LEAVING THE PARENTAL HOME against fast-food intake.

Legal divorce reform interacted with ANCESTRAL MATRILOCALITY in Indonesia, with empowerment as the outcome. The ancestral-residence-rule instrument is a design §4 did not enumerate and could use; the outcome here is not fertility.
No abstract; published version of the Cambodian landmine-amputee study.
Microsimulation parameters for four European welfare regimes.

LIVING-APART-TOGETHER beyond the late twenties in SWEDEN, from the Swedish GGS. The LAT configuration measured in a high-single-household country; relevant to whether partnering and co-residence can be separated.

Married children and their parents in 21st-century Japan, tracing the patrilineal rule under which PARENTS LIVE WITH THE HEIR AND HIS FAMILY from the civil code to the present. The institutional history of the extended configuration in its key setting.
Old-age protection pillars in Hong Kong.
Same Vienna Yearbook debate; the wish for a child.
COVID-19 prevention practices in Ethiopia.
No abstract; COVID-19 mortality by county racial composition.
No abstract; the role of brothers and sisters.
No abstract, but the title is precise: THREE-GENERATION HOUSEHOLDS in the US and THE FIRST EXIT AFTER A CHILD'S BIRTH. The birth precedes the exit -- threat 2 as the explicit object of study. Trace.
'Cool Water' climatic origins of late female marriage and gender egalitarianism. D.2.a's, and another use of 'emancipation' in the gender sense.
Authoritarian parenting and preschool tantrums.
Editorial introduction to the same Vienna Yearbook debate.
No abstract; age at marriage and interval to first birth in Singapore. A.7's.
Essay on race and biology.
Filipino migrant wives in South Korea.
Wittgenstein Centre fertility database description.
Tamang children's elementary education in Nepal.
Policy guidelines for young adults with perinatal HIV in Botswana.
COVID-19 lockdown and family life; multi-day proximity in a limited space is described but not estimated.
Subjective wellbeing among the Chinese oldest-old.
Anticipated living arrangements and care demand among older Chinese living alone.
Migrant Finnish mothers and welfare-state norms.

Living arrangements across 21 EUROPEAN countries from the EU Labour Force Survey, by age and sex, 2006 to 2016, with REGIONAL variation. Harmonised exposure measurement with sub-national resolution -- the denominator the pre-launch arm's descriptive claims need.
Faculty Opinions recommendation of the leaving-home-and-diet paper. A shadow record of an already-screened study.

No abstract; 'A day late and a dollar short: LIQUIDITY AND HOUSEHOLD FORMATION AMONG STUDENT BORROWERS' in the Journal of Financial Economics. C.3.g and C.3.e own the treatment, but it estimates a driver-to-arrangement link with finance-journal identification standards. Report to C.3.g; read for the design.

Microsimulation of HOUSEHOLD AND MARITAL TRANSITIONS leading to CHILDLESSNESS among Dutch women born 1971-2000, motivated by transitions to adulthood becoming late, protracted and complex. The full chain modelled to a fertility endpoint; simulation rather than estimation.
Validation of a parental burnout scale in Basque.
Campbell protocol on involving men in family planning.
Environmental effects of contraceptive pill residues.
One-child-generation Chinese young adults' attitudes to elder care and to LIVING ARRANGEMENT AFTER MARRIAGE. Intentions about the extended configuration in the cohort now forming it.
No abstract; COVID-19 and European paediatric primary care.
